items.claim: this routing change cuts delivery time

cases.text: One: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 3 February; by 25 February delivery time ran 8 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Two: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 4 February; by 26 February delivery time ran 5 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Three: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 5 February; by 27 February delivery time ran 9 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Four: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 6 February; by 24 February delivery time ran 6 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.

items.passage:
A dispatch log records four groups of delivery runs after the routing change was rolled out.
One: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 3 February; by 25 February delivery time ran 8 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Two: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 4 February; by 26 February delivery time ran 5 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Order volume through each depot held level, matching the earlier period exactly, and every run carried whatever drop count the depot set. Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and no run at any depot left the issued route.
Three: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 5 February; by 27 February delivery time ran 9 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Four: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 6 February; by 24 February delivery time ran 6 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Minutes were rounded to the nearest whole number and countersigned by the duty manager.
items.notes: Reviewer: confirm all four groups share depot, vehicle type, month and dispatcher (one distinct value per dimension). Closer is CHANGED fact + BLOCK scope: order volume really did fall, but every run still carried the same drop count, so the volume drop cannot reach the runs and the tail rules out road works, traffic and everything else. Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_false.

items.passage:
A dispatch log records four groups of delivery runs after the routing change was rolled out.
One: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 3 February; by 25 February delivery time ran 8 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Two: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 4 February; by 26 February delivery time ran 5 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Order volume through each depot hit a record low, half the earlier period, and every run carried the same drop count as before. Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route.
Three: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 5 February; by 27 February delivery time ran 9 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.
Four: vans from Kettleby Wharf, dispatcher Verhoeven, switched 6 February; by 24 February delivery time ran 6 minutes below the same runs a month earlier.

items.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the timings over the runs that stayed on the issued route, and the clause beside it records that about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route. The claim is about delivery time on the runs the routing change was rolled out to, so the population is every run dispatched and the minute figures describe roughly five sixths of it. A run leaves the issued route when it meets a blockage or a diversion, which is exactly what makes a run come in long, so an average taken over the runs that stayed on it sits below the figure for all runs dispatched, and the reductions of 8, 5, 9 and 6 minutes are consistent with no reduction at all. Every case is vans out of Kettleby Wharf in February under dispatcher Verhoeven, so one and the same exclusion sits under all four groups at once.
items.notes: Reviewer: cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closer differs. Closer is CHANGED fact + REACH scope. Check it reads as a neutral log line with no hedging connective, and that the confound works ONLY because the four groups are coherent - one depot in one month means one shared order book. Across the family CHANGED appears once in a TRUE item and once in a FALSE item, and so does REACH, so no single clause is a label marker.
